Bug_Title: MC: An overridable method is called from the readObject method. (MC_OVERRIDABLE_METHOD_CALL_IN_READ_OBJECT)
Bug_Details:
The readObject() method must not call any overridable methods. Invoking overridable methods from the readObject()
method can provide the overriding method with access to the object's state before it is fully initialized. This
premature access is possible because, in deserialization, readObject plays the role of object constructor and
therefore object initialization is not complete until readObject exits. 

See SEI CERT rule 
SER09-J. Do not invoke overridable methods from the readObject() method.
Bug_Explanation: The overridable method 'overridableMethod' is called in the readObject method. This is a violation of the rule which states that the readObject method should not call any overridable methods.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the `showBug` method in `OverridableMethodCallBug` class. This method in turn calls the overridable method `overridableMethod` from the `readObject` method in the `OverridableMethodCallBug` class. This is a violation of the rule which states that the readObject method should not call any overridable methods.
